status: MEASURED (Phase 0c). Supersedes the Phase 0 'NOT MEASURED — HTTP 429' state of this file.

measurement_method.formula: tokens = text_bytes (EXACT, from parquet footers over ALL rows) x tokens_per_byte (sampled, dolma2)
measurement_method.why_not_datasets_server: Phase 0 stalled on HTTP 429 because /rows quota is PER-IP, not per-account. Footers are quota-immune: they come off the HF CDN by HTTP Range.
measurement_method.why_a_byte_total_and_not_num_rows_x_mean: the Phase 0 tool multiplied a PARTIAL converted row count by a mean and would have understated stackexchange ~24x. A footer byte total has no such denominator: total_uncompressed_size is summed over every row group of every file.
measurement_method.footer_arithmetic: sum(row_group.column('text').total_uncompressed_size) - 4 bytes/value (PLAIN BYTE_ARRAY length prefix; encodings confirmed PLAIN, correction 0.03-0.23%)
measurement_method.raw_vs_filtered: §3.2 specifies the _filtered corpora, but those repos are .json.gz with ZERO parquet — unmeasurable by footers, which is exactly why Phase 0 could not touch them. common-pile/raw_v0.1_parquet carries the RAW collection as parquet, so RAW is measured exactly and scaled to filtered by the cards' own byte ratio. Both figures are reported per source.

transfer_budget.note: §5.7 honoured — no dataset download; footers + sampled column chunks only, nothing written to disk (disk at 92%)

CRITICAL_TRAP_FOUND.severity: HIGH — a naive footer read of raw_v0.1_parquet overstates ubuntu_irc 2.1x and github_archive 4.5x
CRITICAL_TRAP_FOUND.what: For ubuntu_irc and github_archive the consolidated parquet swept TWO document trees from the source repo. Its `text` byte total is therefore a SUPERSET of the corpus the card describes.

evidence_ubuntu_irc.source_repo_has: raw/documents (8 files, 2.44 GB gz) AND v0/documents (8 files, 2.24 GB gz)
evidence_ubuntu_irc.id_level_proof: read the FULL id column (2.95 MB): 1,062,264 rows -> 733,149 distinct; the copies-per-id histogram is EXACTLY {1: 404034, 2: 329115} and 329,115 IS the raw card's document count — i.e. one whole tree is duplicated inside the other

evidence_github_archive.source_repo_has: gharchive/raw/documents (2000 files, 65.16 GB gz) AND gharchive/v0/documents (2000 files, 18.69 GB gz)
evidence_github_archive.id_level_proof: ZERO duplicate ids across sampled row groups — so unlike ubuntu_irc this is not a duplicate, it is a genuinely LARGER pre-filter row set (177M threads before license filtering, per the card). The overshoot is real extra rows, not double-counting.

CRITICAL_TRAP_FOUND.correction_applied: scale the footer total by the v0 tree's share of gz bytes. This reproduces each RAW card independently: ubuntu_irc 6.39 vs 6.3 GB (+1.47%), github_archive 55.05 vs 54.7 GB (+0.64%). stackexchange has ONE tree and needed no correction: 104.98 vs 103.7 GB (+1.24%).
CRITICAL_TRAP_FOUND.why_it_would_pass_unnoticed: nothing in a footer read reveals it; the byte total is internally consistent and the corpus is the one you asked for by name. Only the card disagreement exposes it.
CRITICAL_TRAP_FOUND.affects_other_agents: ANY Phase 0c agent footer-counting common-pile/raw_v0.1_parquet must check its source repo for a second document tree. stackv2 (415 files), cccc (87), peS2o (58), uspto (116) are all large enough for this to matter.

card_unit_resolved.question: is Common Pile's 'UTF-8 GB' 10^9 bytes or GiB?
card_unit_resolved.how: ubuntu_irc_filtered is the one corpus here whose datasets-server parquet conversion is COMPLETE, so its footer byte total is exact: 5,292,175,174 B. Card says 5.3 GB -> -0.15% as 10^9, -7.01% as GiB.
card_unit_resolved.consequence: the card GB ratios used for raw->filtered scaling are unit-consistent with our bytes

sa_split.measured_how: per-document metadata.license on 1,600 sampled docs across the two counted sources: stackexchange 800/800 CC-BY-SA (3.0 51.4% / 4.0 45.3% / 2.5 3.3% by tokens), ubuntu_irc 800/800 Public Domain. NOT inferred from the cards, which carry no license field.
sa_split.confirms_phase0: §7 item 4 treated SA as a footnote; Phase 0 called it structural. Measured: 92.8% of this category's tokens are CC-BY-SA.

if_SA_dropped.verdict: FAILS the 3x floor at 0.26x, and fails the 2.4B peak itself at 0.78x
if_SA_dropped.the_fix_is_github_archive: adding github_archive_filtered's 11.511B non-SA tokens brings the SA-free pool to 13.386B = 1.86x the floor, which PASSES. github_archive is the only reason a share-alike-free QA/forum pool is feasible at all — that, not the token count, is the strongest argument for classifying it here.

sa_split.actionable: make share-alike a first-class queryable `label` on every entry before first publish. entry.labels is inside manifest_sha256 and is therefore UNBACKFILLABLE (see memory); a later 'strip SA and re-mix' must be a metadata query, not a re-copy.

category_verdict_github_archive.verdict: It is QA/forum by content, and it should be BUDGETED to QA/forum, not code.
category_verdict_github_archive.evidence_content: the `source` field on all 824 sampled documents is gharchive/issue (484) or gharchive/pull-request (340) — GitHub issue/PR threads. Its own card describes PyMarkdown-flattened issue and PR comment threads, not source files. Mean doc 1,981 bytes / median 894 — comment-thread length, not file length.
category_verdict_github_archive.evidence_tokenizer: 0.2831 tok/byte sits between StackExchange prose-Q&A (0.2649) and IRC dialogue (0.3486), and NOWHERE near a code corpus; §3.2's code row cites stackv2_edu at 0.274 tok/char. Its per-doc spread (2.45x) matches StackExchange's (2.39x) — the same prose+code-block interleaving.
category_verdict_github_archive.the_decisive_argument: code's pool does not need it (stackv2_edu alone floors at 61-80B against a 40B pool), whereas QA/forum's SA-free pool CANNOT meet its floor without it (1.875B = 0.26x). Assigning it to code leaves a measured license risk unmitigated to pad a pool that is already met.
category_verdict_github_archive.double_counting_guard: it must be counted ONCE. Our category_total EXCLUDES it, so no double count exists today; if it moves here, `code` must drop it from its own table in the same edit.
category_verdict_github_archive.reconcile_with: artifacts/recount/code-github-archive-filtered.json and code.json — the code agent measured the same corpus; the two numbers should be compared before §3.2 is rewritten.

method_caveat_this_category_confirmed.phase0_warning: Phase 0 measured 0.4524 vs 0.2101 tok/char on two documents (2.15x) and warned the single-ratio estimator is weaker here than on prose.
method_caveat_this_category_confirmed.measured_at_scale: CONFIRMED but BOUNDED. Per-document spread is 2.39x (stackexchange), 2.45x (github_archive), 4.65x (ubuntu_irc) — Phase 0's 2.15x was, if anything, an underestimate of the tails. Per-document CV 0.135 / 0.150 / 0.116.
method_caveat_this_category_confirmed.why_the_estimate_survives_it: per-document variance is NOT the uncertainty on a corpus-level ratio. Aggregating byte-weighted over 800+ docs in 32-33 independent row groups, the between-row-group CV falls to 0.107 / 0.073 / 0.027 and CI95 to +-3.6% / +-2.5% / +-0.9%.
method_caveat_this_category_confirmed.how_much_weaker_plainly: the QA/forum ratio is ~4x less precise than a prose corpus's would be (+-3.6% vs the ~+-1% typical of English prose), so the category total should be read as 25.9B +- ~1B on the ratio alone. That is nowhere near the 2.16x margin over the plan pool, so the sizing verdict is robust; a re-weighting decision at the 5% level would not be.

head_bias_cross_check.question: the tok/byte ratio is sampled from the datasets-server-CONVERTED _filtered parquet, which covers only 4.7% (stackexchange) / 10.7% (github_archive) of rows. Is that head a biased sample?
head_bias_cross_check.why_it_was_a_real_worry: the StackExchange source repo is laid out ONE DIRECTORY PER SITE in alphabetical order, and stackoverflow.com (95 of 835 files) is both the largest site and the most code-dense. Code raises tok/byte sharply, so a head that stops before 's' would yield a PROSE-SITE ratio and understate the corpus.
head_bias_cross_check.test: an independent tok/byte sample drawn from common-pile/raw_v0.1_parquet, whose row set covers ALL 34.0M / 139.7M rows and therefore every site, at random row groups across distinct files.
head_bias_cross_check.verdict: No material bias. Both divergences (+2.7%, +7.9%) sit inside the overlapping CI95 bands of the two independent samples, and BOTH point the same way — the full-corpus ratio is slightly HIGHER than the head's, so the head-based figures reported above are CONSERVATIVE (they understate tokens).
head_bias_cross_check.which_ratio_the_headline_uses: the HEAD (converted _filtered) ratio, deliberately: it is drawn from the correct FILTERED row set and it is the lower of the two. Substituting the raw ratios would raise the category total from 25.93B to ~26.6B and would not change any verdict.
head_bias_cross_check.residual_caveat: the raw-repo sample is cheap in requests but expensive in bytes (that repo writes 40k-120k-row row groups, so 700 docs cost 607 MB vs 74 MB for 800 docs from the converted parquet), hence its smaller row-group count (14 / 10) and wider CI.
